category_title: Agentive multilingual learners who view dialogue as a collaborative space for sharing ideas
minimal_context: The student is participating in a small group discussion at an oval-shaped table to answer a question about the importance of science using page 285 of the text.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's answer the question: How does George describe the importance of science to the audience? Please use page 285 of the text.

STUDENT: If we didn’t have science, we wouldn’t understand the universe and we wouldn’t make good decisions, or how science could be really important to us so that we can make our future better.

TUTOR: Okay. What else does it say?

STUDENT: And on 285 [Begins reading from the book] I wanted to tell you about it because science is really important.

TUTOR: Why do you think we are discussing this in a small group?

STUDENT: Because maybe one of our members may have the right answer? [2 second pause] Or maybe she wants us to share ideas with one another.

options.A: Building personal relationships outside of the classroom by visiting the student and her family at home.
options.B: Asking follow-up questions to model conversational skills during the small group discussion.
options.C: Using specific conceptual questions with a limited range of possible answers rather than broad, open-ended questions.
options.D: Instituting a classroom norm of assigning a different colored post-it to each group member.
